text:
Overall, I find this game pretty enjoyable and, if you're new to the Payday series, I would recommend staring with Payday 3 over 2. My reason for that being, this game is much more clear on what to do with specific mechanics that are easily missed by new players (myself included). Also, the updated controls and movement make it hard to go back to Payday 2.

Pros
-The gunplay is much tighter in Payday 3
-The movement QoL feels really good
-Objectives are clearer
-The updated visuals look amazing.
-A lot more ways to customize your controls.
-Bots feel a little bit more useful compared to Payday 2.

gameplay.evidence: this game is much more clear on what to do with specific mechanics

controls.evidence: Also, the updated controls and movement make it hard to go back to Payday 2.

text:
Absolute Masterpiece! (9/10)
​Hollow Knight is a breathtaking journey through a beautifully dark and tragic world. Everything in this game comes together perfectly to create an unforgettable experience:
​Gameplay & Combat: Silky-smooth mechanics, tight controls, and rewarding progression.
​Music & Atmosphere: The soundtrack and visual design are hauntingly beautiful, drawing you deep into the lore of Hallownest.
​Challenge: The difficulty is tough and demanding, but incredibly satisfying to master.
​Final Score: 9 / 10
The only reason it’s not a full 10/10 is the lack of official Arabic lauage support. Other than that, it is near perfection. Highly recommended to anyone who loves Metroidvanias and great storytelling!

text: The gameplay is fun, albeit somewhat easy for people familiar with the mechanics, and the monster roster is very good. text:
RDR2 is a masterpiece in world-building, atmosphere, storytelling and immersion, which makes its controls all the more frustrating.

For a game so heavily focused on cinematic immersion, the clunky, sluggish and overly complicated controls constantly pull you out of the experience. Too many context-sensitive actions, too much input delay, too much fighting the character instead of simply controlling him.

It’s still an incredible game, but Rockstar’s refusal to properly adapt the controls for PC is a baffling design failure. Such a shame

Warzone is an absolute joke at this point. The servers are some of the worst I've ever seen in a major online game. Constant lag, packet bursts, desync, random disconnects, and getting killed around corners make every match feel broken. It doesn't matter how good your aim or positioning is when the servers decide who wins the fight.

What's even worse is the endless plague of cheaters. Every other match seems to have someone with suspicious tracking, wallhacks, or blatant aimbotting. It's beyond frustrating to spend 20 minutes looting and fighting just to get wiped by someone who clearly isn't playing legitimately. The anti-cheat system feels completely ineffective.

This game is honestly really fun. The characters are great, and playing as Mastermind is the best part for me. Setting traps, controlling creatures, and wiping out survivors never gets old. It feels satisfying when your plans actually work and the survivors panic trying to escape.

Survivor mode is alright too, but sometimes the survivors can be really annoying to deal with. Even then, the chaos makes matches exciting. I’m pretty sure most people who play Mastermind know how enjoyable it is once you learn how to control the match properly.

Overall, despite its flaws, this game is still a very fun multiplayer experience and deserves more attention. If you enjoy strategy, chaos, and messing with survivors, Mastermind gameplay is absolutely worth it.

text:
Fantastic game

Capcom made a game that is essentially two games in one. They somehow managed to make a horror survival game and an action game, where each alone are top tier in their respective genres, and also made it so that they switch back and fourth and mesh excellently. The Grace sections make you feel weak and scared while you have to be resourceful while the Leon sections make you feel like an unstoppable bad ass.

The graphics looked very good, the difficulty I played at, Standard (Modern), wasn't too challenging, but was still engaging, the story was cool, the references to the series past was fun, and overall just a fantastic time that didn't overstay it's welcome.

The only thing I would have liked to see were more puzzles.

text:
For a game as cheap as a dollar, the value is insane as the modding community is alive and well. text:
Honestly, after waiting for what felt like forever, stepping into Pharloom as Hornet was worth every single second. I’m definitely not the most skilled gamer out there I died way more times than I’d like to admit but Hollow Knight: Silksong is an absolute masterpiece.

The movement feels so fluid and acrobatic compared to the original. Jumping, sprinting, and using Hornet’s needle craft makes combat feel like a fast-paced dance. The handcrafted art style, atmospheric music, and intricate world design continually blew me away. Every new area had me completely immersed, even when a brutal boss had me stuck for an hour.

It’s tough, but every victory feels earned and ridiculously satisfying. If you enjoy action platformers, atmospheric worlds, or just a really solid challenge, I can't recommend this game enough. Do yourself a favor and give it a play you won't regret it!

text:
I'm not saying this lightly, but I just cannot recommend this game. It's hard and tedious instead of hard but fun, unlike the previous installment. Underrewarding and constantly demanding, without ever giving you a break to explore the gorgeous world. It has its merits of course - graphics are lovely and detailed, music is beutiful and adds to the atmosphere, but I'm stating the obvious here. However, when the game frustrates me way more than it gives me satisfaction or a sense of wonder, then I'm afraid I'm done with the game. And Silksong happily shows me a middle finger at every step. As a Hollow Knight fan, I am disappointed. I wanted to love this game, but it simply wouldn't let me.
Say "skill issue" or whatever, I don't care.

Better than it's predecessor IMO.

Still, some issues remain such as the devs insistence on giving almost all enemies contact damage even when some of them really don't need it, and they clearly understand that some enemies work better without it.

There's also the fact that 100% completion is nigh-impossible without either resorting to online resources or sweeping the entire map while attacking every wall and jumping into every ceiling.

But at the end of the day it's still really, really good. It definitely deserved it's GOTY nomination... if it came out a year earlier it probably would've won.

text:
I don't think RDR2 should be approached like most games. If I'm being honest, some of the gameplay is garbage. The horse controls can be annoying and there's no shortage of bugs. But you're not here for game mechanics. You're here for the delivery of a masterfully written story that uses a video game as its vessel.

text: The base game is outstanding but Leon Must Die Forever is the worst extra mode I've ever played in a Resident Evil game. It's like playing a slot machine, you have zero control over the outcome, you just waste time losing over and over again until you get good RNG via perks to counter the ridiculous levels of artificial difficulty.

I loved RE7. RE8, however, was massively overhyped. Thankfully, RE9 is a return to form.

Let's start with the positives.

+It looks great.
+Runs well and is properly optimised.
+Crunchier, more satisfying combat with much better weapon sounds.
+More memorable than RE8, with stronger writing.
+An overall far more enjoyable experience than RE8.

Now the negatives.

-Grace's voice acting gets annoying with her constant stammering.
-Leon's voice actor sounds bored at times, although I suppose that's just part of his badass persona?
-Nerfed dismemberment compared to previous games.
-Still no f*****g FOV slider. Seriously, Capcom?

Overall, RE9 is a massive improvement over RE8. Better combat, better presentation, better writing, and a much more memorable experience. It's not perfect, but Capcom cooked - mostly.

text:
Well, well…

This game’s multiplayer is as empty as an Elon Musk book-signing session on a Monday morning.

The co-op mode doesn’t exist – not because Capcom have thrown in some zombies, but because there’s no way to team up with your mates to fight them.

The only single-player mode available is a survival mode consisting of missions and… it’s absolutely rubbish.

The gameplay is worse than a PS1 game without a DualShock; a controller is strongly recommended, even though it’s still a right pain.

Apart from that, the game looks very nice for a Unity title.

So clearly, if you want a zombie game, look elsewhere, because even for €1 I’d be bored stiff, so avoid it at €15 on Steam

I will dig in my heels & defend the voice acting, music & art style. It's a 5/5 on atmosphere, it is a true WH40K game. But at the end of the day, gameplay rules with an iron fist & trying to merge the 2 previous games constitutions was poorly executed, if it was possible in the first place.

If you want good feels, this knocked it out of the park. But if you want a good game? only if you're ok with overpaying...

text:
I like it, rating it 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐. A lot busier than the other Dawn of War titles. Feels like you're commanding an actual big army this time. Also base-building is improved compared to Dawn of War 2, but still not as robust as OG Dawn of War. Audio and voice overs are great too. Makes you feel the urgency.

Also the power scaling of hero units, plus the tower system during skirmishes gives it a MOBA vibe. Makes it harder to zerg rush, which ngl in the earlier Dawn of War series is doable in some scenarios.

Not 5 star because of the cluttered UI. It takes some getting used to but needlessly complicated.
